title: Generator-normalized tensor comparison for a ringed-site slice
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, $O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $V\in\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Use the localized ringed site with $O_V(W,f)=O(W)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and exact extension $j_!\dashv j^*$ [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For an $O_V$-module sheaf $G$ and an $O$-module sheaf $H$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], write $[x]_f$ for the image under module sheafification of $x\in G(W,f)$ in the summand indexed by $f:W\to V$ of the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

There is a unique $O$-linear map
$$\psi_{G,H}:j_!G\otimes_OH\longrightarrow j_!(G\otimes_{O_V}j^*H)$$
whose composite on each pair of original presheaf sections is $[x]_f\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_{(W,f)}]_f$. It is an isomorphism, natural in both module morphisms. Its inverse $\kappa_{G,H}$ is the $j_!\dashv j^*$-adjunct of
$$G\otimes j^*H\xrightarrow{\eta_G\otimes1}j^*j_!G\otimes j^*H\cong j^*(j_!G\otimes H),$$
where $\eta$ is the actual extension-presheaf adjunction unit and the last isomorphism is the pure-tensor restriction comparison [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]. On original sections $\eta_G(x)=[x]_f$ and $\kappa([x\otimes a]_f)=[x]_f\otimes a$. Both inverse identities are identities of sheaf maps with these prescribed generators, not just an existence of an unnormalized tensor isomorphism. No flatness or constant-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the prescribed unit equation of the actual extension/restriction adjunction. Adjunction then identifies evaluation of the adjunct of f at x with f([x]_φ). This proves extensionality on original extension sections, and naturality of these sections in the slice module and under restriction.

At V distribute the tensor of the extension direct sum with H(V) using Mathlib TensorProduct.directSumLeft. On the φ summand apply the slice tensor sheafification unit and then the extension sheafification unit. The resulting linear maps send i_φ(x) tensor a to [x tensor a]_φ. Restrictions preserve this formula: use direct-sum induction and tensor induction, allowing colliding indices to add. This constructs a morphism from the tensor presheaf to the extension of the slice tensor.

The module sheafification unit of the extension presheaf is locally bijective. By lem-weil-pbc-tensor-local-bijection-universes, its tensor with the identity of H becomes invertible after sheafification. Compose its inverse with the sheafification adjunct of the previous presheaf morphism to obtain psi. Naturality of the sheafification unit gives the stated generator formula. Cancellation of this invertible map, followed by the sheafification adjunction, tensor induction and direct-sum induction, proves that maps out of j_!G tensor H are detected on [x]_φ tensor a.

Define kappa to be the inverse adjunction image of (eta_G tensor id) followed by the inverse of the prescribed restriction comparison. Its formula on extended slice pure tensors follows from the adjunct formula, the normalized unit and the normalized restriction comparison.

The composite psi followed by kappa fixes [x]_φ tensor a, so extension-tensor extensionality proves the first inverse identity. For the other identity apply extension adjunction and slice tensor extensionality: both maps agree on all x tensor a by their two generator formulas. Assemble these maps and identities into an isomorphism.

The forward generator formula and extension-tensor extensionality give uniqueness. For g and h both naturality composites send [x]_φ tensor a to [g(x) tensor h(a)]_φ, using naturality of the tensor and extension sheafification units. This proves naturality in both variables. The inverse is the specified adjunct by construction, and the last clause is the normalized unit equation.

Step 1 builds the actual adjunction from the extension-presheaf and sheafification definitions and gets η(x)=[x]_f. Step 3 applies bilinear extension with O^#=O and H^#≅H, then the tensor bijection, and gets existence and uniqueness. Step 4 gets κ([t]_f)=q(t) for every section t, using lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction (pure tensors to pure tensors, no flatness). Step 5 proves κψ=1 by comparing pairings on summand generators and extending uniquely; no sheaf section is assumed to lift. Step 6 proves ψκ=1 by taking adjuncts and applying the tensor universal property on C/V, where G and j*H are sheaves, so every section is tested. Step 7 proves naturality by the same uniqueness. Edge cases checked: Hom(W,V) empty, several arrows W→V, H=O, zero modules, trivial topology.
